sections.content:
Owner intent (2026-07-31): SRS does not grow internal RAG. A companion standard for full addressable RAG will be established alongside SRS; the small-scale version inside SRS is embedded sources (source-documents/ + .meta.json sidecars, RFC-023 sourceRefs, RFC-017 attachments) plus lexical discovery (ext:discovery find, agent-index, MCP resources) — genuinely sufficient at hundreds-of-instances scale with zero infrastructure.

WHY (lineage evidence): SemOps v2 (semops2, an SRS ancestor) baked ChunkingConfig / ProcessingPipeline / StorageConfig — chunk overlap, embedding models, storage backends — into its core schema (schema/semops/v1/knowledge.proto), welding ML-infrastructure churn to a semantics standard. The charter's out-of-scope list ('a storage engine, database, or sync service — SRS is a portable format, not infrastructure') is the corrective; the companion split is the charter applied. SemOps v1 (the products vault) got the split right in practice: curated sources lived in the vault, retrieval machinery (the brain MCP chat service) lived entirely outside it.

THE SEAM — what the companion CONSUMES from SRS: (1) stable addresses into content — ext:addressability (instance, field, revision); (2) the canonical text to index — ext:discovery's deterministic Text Projection, normative for all three tiers, solving 'what exactly did we embed'; (3) provenance edges back — sourceRefs, derived-from; (4) change detection — checksums, revisions.

What the companion OWNS and SRS never absorbs: chunking, embeddings, vector storage, retrieval APIs, ranking.

KEYSTONE PROPERTY: retrieval citations resolve to SRS addresses — v1's 'verifiable sources is a human job' discipline made machine-checkable.

When RAG/embedding/vector features are proposed for core, cite this note and the charter out-of-scope list; route to the companion standard. Graduate to a design-note record when the companion standard is chartered.
